Subject: MAP: Data handling & compliance milestone — draft and next steps

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the data handling & compliance milestone so your legal and engineering teams can validate assumptions. Quick recap of the milestone we discussed:

- Milestone: Data handling & compliance — covers retention, logging/audit trails, data classification (PHI/PII), and export controls.
- Target close date: 2026-06-30 (customer prefers end of month close; we proposed two-week DPA review cadence).
- Responsibilities:
  - MedTech Co: confirm retention windows, provide sample data classification policy, legal to review DPA & data processing controls.
  - Redwood: deliver MAP draft v1 (attached), provide SOC 2 artifacts (redacted), outline retention/config options and audit log capability.
- Dependencies: final DPA, legal sign-off, SOC 2 evidence review, any required encryption/KMS integration.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm whether MedTech will require PHI handling (HIPAA) coverage for this integration? If yes we should loop in your compliance lead and surface BAA requirements.
2) Please share an agreed retention window for training and inference logs (default Redwood proposal in the MAP draft is configurable 30/90/365 days).
3) Any blocking vendor-specific legal language (e.g., data localization, export controls) we should surface now?

Attachments: MedTech-MAP-v1.xlsx, SOC2_AICPA_report_redacted.pdf

I'll follow up with a short internal note to engineering/legal and propose a 30-minute sync next week to finalize the MAP items.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance milestone — draft and next steps

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap and appreciate the draft MAP. A few quick points from our side:

- We are a healthcare device company and the data scope for this pilot will include device telemetry and user-reported outcomes. There is potential PHI (patient identifiers) in the telemetry payloads unless we pseudonymize. We need to treat this as a HIPAA-sensitive integration until legal confirms otherwise.
- Retention: for the pilot, our compliance team would prefer 90 days for inference logs and 365 days for audit logs; training data must be opt-in and only with explicit approvals.
- Encryption: at-rest encryption with customer-managed KMS is preferred.
- We will need to review a BAA if PHI is confirmed.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood supports per-customer KMS and whether audit logs can be ingested to our Splunk instance (SaaS forwarding)? Also please confirm whether Redwood performs any automated model-training on customer data by default (we expect no training without explicit consent).

Would be great to schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week with your engineering and our compliance/legal leads.

Thanks,
Sara Lewis
Head of Product Partnerships | MedTech Co
[sara.lewis@medtechco.com]

Sara —

Thanks for the quick clarifications — very helpful. Quick responses inline and an updated set of proposed MAP milestones below. I also attached MAP v1 with the retention & responsibilities updated per your ask.

- PHI/BAA: Treating this as HIPAA-sensitive for now. We'll plan to provision a BAA and will include standard HIPAA controls in the DPA. Can your legal share the right contact?
- Retention: Updated proposal in MAP v1: inference logs = 90 days (configurable), audit logs = 365 days (exportable), training data only stored if MedTech explicitly opts in.
- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and for Dedicated customers; for Hosted we support BYOK integrations for keys in supported cloud providers. I asked engineering to confirm feasible setup for your environment.
- No automated model training: Redwood does not use customer inference traffic to train public models by default. Training from customer data is explicit and opt-in and documented in the DPA.

Proposed MAP milestone (high-level):
1) Legal review: MedTech legal to review DPA & BAA (target review complete: 2026-06-07) — owner: MedTech Legal
2) Engineering alignment: confirm KMS & Splunk export approach (target complete: 2026-06-14) — owner: Redwood Engineering (Vivek)
3) Finalize MAP & sign DPA/BAA (target complete: 2026-06-30) — owner: jointly Redwood & MedTech

Dependencies: MedTech to share compliance contact and sample data classification; Redwood to provide SOC2 artifacts and confirm KMS/Splunk export technical approach.

Next steps:
- Vivek, can you confirm per-customer KMS support details and whether we can stream audit logs to a customer Splunk instance (SaaS forward)?
- Neha, I'll follow up with a draft DPA language we usually provide for HIPAA customers.
- Sara, can you suggest 2x 30-minute slots next week for a working session with your compliance lead?

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance milestone — draft and next steps

Adding engineering detail here so legal/compliance have the technical options spelled out. Short summary:

- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted, we offer BYOK via cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) with per-tenant keys for key isolation. For HIPAA customers we recommend Dedicated or Private if you require strict key control.
- Retention storage: retention windows are configurable per-tenant; default infra retention for ephemeral KV/cache is 30 days, but we can expose 90/365 options as needed. We can also provide a policy to purge inference payloads and training samples on demand.
- Audit logs: we can export structured audit logs (JSON events) to an S3 bucket or stream events to a customer-managed SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via secure forwarder. Logs include request metadata, model id, timestamps, and operator actions; payload-level filtering/pseudonymization is configurable.
- PHI handling: we do not use production inference data for model retraining by default. If a customer opts into training, that is a separate workflow with controls documented in the DPA and opt-in audited.

I'll coordinate with product to provide an architecture note and a small runbook for Splunk forwarding by 2026-06-04. If any of this is a blocking requirement please flag and we can escalate to solutions engineering for a PoC.

— Vivek
Principal Engineer, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
